lead: St. Louis has some of the oldest brick housing in the country, plus flash floods and river floods. DryFlare helps homes from Soulard to Carondelet dry out properly.
risk: flash flooding, basement backups and leaks in century-old homes
why: On July 26, 2022, about nine inches of rain fell on St. Louis in a few hours, a record that flooded homes, highways and basements across the city and county. The River Des Peres overflowed in south St. Louis. In 1993, the downtown floodwall held back a record Mississippi crest.

Nearly 58% of St. Louis homes were built before 1940, more than any other big U.S. city. Brick homes and flats have stone foundations, old cast-iron drains and plaster walls. Old combined sewers back up in storms, and winter cold bursts old pipes.
image_alt: Water covering the floor of an old brick basement
image_caption: Century-old St. Louis basements took in water across the city in the 2022 flood.
problems: River Des Peres and low areas
tips: Install a backwater valve if your basement has a drain.
Ask MSD about backup prevention programs.
areas: Calls come from Soulard, the Central West End, Tower Grove, the Hill, Lafayette Square, Dogtown and Carondelet, plus Clayton, Kirkwood, Webster Groves, Florissant and St. Charles.

faq.q: How did the 2022 St. Louis flood happen?
faq.a: Storms trained over the city on July 26, 2022, dropping about nine inches of rain in a few hours. Sewers and creeks couldn't keep up, and water flooded homes and roads. Flood insurance covers that kind of rising water.
